history.dynasty: Chola (current structure mainly 12th-13th century); patronage/renovations by Pallava, Chola, Pandya, Vijayanagara and Chera royals
history.period: Medieval (12th-13th century current structure; worship from the classical period)
history.summary: The Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram is one of the foremost temples of Shaivism, influencing worship, architecture, sculpture and performance art for over two millennia. Shiva is worshipped here as Nataraja, the cosmic dancer — one of the few temples where Shiva takes anthropomorphic form rather than the classic lingam. It is the Akasha (space/sky) shrine of the Pancha Bhoota Stalams, and 'Chidambaram' is read as 'chit' (consciousness) + 'ambaram' (sky). History: a major Shiva shrine since the classical period; the present complex is mainly 12th-13th century Chola, with gold-plated gopurams added by royals including Aditya I, Parantaka I, Kopperunchinga I, Krishnadevaraya and Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan. King Kocengannan Chola (born following prayers his parents offered at this temple) refined its structure. The temple gave the town its name (Thillai = the mangrove forest of Excoecaria agallocha in which it stood). Features: the five sabhas (Chit, Kanaka, Deva, Nritya, Raja) with Nataraja in the Chit Sabha; the four gopurams carved with the 108 karanas of Natya Shastra; the Chidambara Rahasyam (formless aspect of Shiva); and the Ponnambalam gold hall.

name: Thillai Nataraja Temple
town_description: Chidambaram is a temple town in Cuddalore district, east-central Tamil Nadu, about 235 km from Chennai. The Nataraja temple complex (about 40 acres) occupies the heart of the town; the town itself is named after the shrine.

travel.airport: Chennai International Airport — about 235 km; Pondicherry — about 65 km (verify).
travel.railway: Chidambaram railway station — about 1.5 km from the temple (verify).
travel.road: In the heart of Chidambaram town; on the Chidambaram-Thanjavur highway, well connected by buses from Chennai, Kumbakonam and Thanjavur.

visitor_information.best_time: December to February for pleasant weather; December-January for Margazhi Thiruvathirai; February-March for the Natyanjali dance festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM; 5:00 PM to 10:00 PM (verify locally; timings vary between sources). Entry free.
